We need to find a Costas array of order 5 with x[2]=3. A Costas array is a permutation of {0,...,n-1} such that the displacement vectors between pairs of marks are all distinct. Specifically, for columns i<j, the vector is (x[j]-x[i], j-i). Since j-i > 0, we require all these vectors to be distinct. Equivalently, for any two pairs (i,j) and (k,l) with i<j and k<l and (i,j) != (k,l), we must have (x[j]-x[i], j-i) != (x[l]-x[k], l-k). Since the second component is the column difference, if j-i != l-k then the vectors are automatically distinct. So we only need to worry about pairs with the same column difference d = j-i = l-k. For each d from 1 to n-1, the differences x[i+d]-x[i] for i=0..n-1-d must all be distinct. This is the standard definition: for each d, the set {x[i+d]-x[i] | i=0..n-1-d} has size n-d.
